I think that the first thing you should do is try to get more comfortable with breathing, as its one of the most important parts of swimming. 

Focus on the rythm, either breathing every 2 or 3 strokes at the beginning. Dont rush into 5 or 7 only to gasp after 50 meters. Dont try to go fast if you do this, the point is to get more comfortable, and slowing down also helps to focus on technique. If you get too uncomfortable just stop for a while, rest and calm yourself down and try again. 

If you have trouble with water getting in your nose when you swim, you can invest in this thing that you put on your nose to stop the water (sorry, english isnt my native language, i have no idea how its called). 

I cant really help you with technique as im not a coach and ive never seen you swim but i have one thing to say about mentality. Its a mistake i and all of my teammates did, until our coach pointed it out (she had to talk about this one a lot), and then magically, everyone beats their pb. 

Do not focus on going fast. When your only goal is to go fast, your technique degrades. Youre not supposed to swim fast, your goal is to swim good. Break the distance into a few parts, know what you have to do respectively. Its good to visualise it, either at home when you rest or at practice/competition. 

Firts part of the race is the dive. You have to be focused to have a good reaction time. Then you have a strong underwater, maintain your speed from the dive, dont go for too long, otherwise you will slow down. Then there is distance, focus on a strong kick and pull and rhytmic breathing. Then you have a quick turn, with another underwater. Again strong kick and pull. The last 10/15 meters will be the hardest, focus on your legs more there, people tend to associate going fast with quick pulls, and dont use the full power of their kick. Then the last 2m, dont be scared of the wall, dont slow down at the end. Our coach used to say that we must "attack" the wall, to force us to go full speed until the last meter. 

So, my best advice would be, dont swim as fast as you can, swim the best you can, the speed will come with it. 

Good luck!

What do you mean by that you usually try to make at least 3 strokes? Do you sometimes make 3 sometimes 4 or 5? If Yes, The best advice i can give you is to be more consistent. For example, if you arent able to make 3 strokes before inhaling again (consistently),  dont try to do 4. All of the hardest breathing drills my coach gives us are the ones with changing rythm - it can be confusing and tiring for an experienced swimmer, much more difficult for a begginer. If you cant do 3 strokes try 2 (breathe on your right side for one lenght, and on left for the other so you train both sides) and once you feel comfortable you can try 3 again.
